// about 01

Computer Science student learning applied machine learning and offensive security, with an interest in how they connect.

I’m a Computer Science student at Benha National University, majoring in AI/ML and Cybersecurity. Right now I’m training at CIB, getting a real look at how banking systems work and where AI actually fits into that world — alongside studying penetration testing and application security at NTI. Before that, I went through a full CCNA track: routers, switches, VLANs, the fundamentals of keeping a network secure. Outside of class, I keep digging into machine learning and red-team methodology, then try to actually build something with it instead of just reading about it.

// projects 04

~/loan-approval-prediction
python scikit-learn pandas machine learning

Built to really understand the ML workflow end to end — cleaning financial data, encoding categorical features, then training Logistic Regression and Decision Tree models to compare how each one predicts loan approval.

~/linux-information
bash linux automation recon

A Bash project born out of learning the language itself — it pulls system info, CPU/memory/disk usage, network config, and open ports, then packages it all into one clean report.

~/blackbox
python network recon port scanning cli

A lightweight Python network reconnaissance framework built for NTI's Penetration Testing & Application Security program — CIDR network discovery, TCP port scanning, and DNS lookups, all wrapped in an interactive CLI and backed by 37 passing automated tests, with more features on the way.

Open to internshipsin AI/ML & cybersecurity
My three weeks in the 2026 Summer Internship Program with CIB Egypt taught me more than I expected. It wasn't just about banking; I also learned how to think, evolve, and lead in a world shaped by artificial intelligence. Here's what really stuck with me: AI is a thinking partner, not a decision-maker. From generative AI and color-based evaluation models to active AI, I learned that true skill lies not in using the tool, but in knowing when to question it. Technology has an environmental cost. Training a single AI model can consume millions of liters of water. Technological literacy also means responsibility. Be skeptical, not pessimistic. The PIQPACC framework changed how I approach any information, whether it's AI-generated or human-made. (Knowledge + Skills) × Attitude = Your True Professional Value No matter how advanced your technical skills are, your mindset is what multiplies everything.
